research_question: Can reducing per-call Q.ANT accumulation width improve reference-to-Q.ANT agreement in a trained FashionMNIST Fourier classifier without materially reducing reference accuracy?
observations: Exp021 found a strong synthetic relationship between accumulated-term count and Q.ANT CPU-backend numerical error, with log-log R2 approximately 0.953.
A monolithic g4 FashionMNIST QFourier layer accumulates 784 x 4 terms per output in one KAN call.
Partitioning the 784 inputs into groups reduces per-call fan-in while retaining all input pixels and the same four Fourier frequencies.
hypothesis: Grouped g4 architectures with smaller per-call input fan-in will reduce reference-to-Q.ANT logit error and prediction disagreements relative to monolithic g4, while retaining similar reference accuracy.
falsification_criterion: The hypothesis is weakened if grouping does not reduce mean absolute logit error and prediction disagreements consistently across seeds, or if any reduction requires a material loss of reference accuracy.

proposed_method.group_combination: sum per-group class logits plus one shared bias

limitations: CPU backend only; no photonic hardware performance claim.
Grouped execution changes numerical evaluation order but intentionally preserves the additive exact-cosine function class and parameter count.
This experiment tests numerical compatibility, not latency, energy efficiency or throughput.
